```js

expect.note: qs 6.14.2 is the top-level copy used by express's query parser, which calls only qs.parse(str,{allowPrototypes:true}) (express lib/utils.js:288-291). The bug is in qs.stringify with arrayFormat:'comma' + encodeValuesOnly, which nothing in the app or its runtime dependencies calls.

qs v6.15.3

facts.advisory_summary:
qs: Denial of Service via Attacker Controlled isBuffer — ### Summary

`qs.stringify()` calls `utils.isBuffer()` on every value it serializes, and `utils.isBuffer()` invokes `obj.constructor.isBuffer(obj)` without checking that it is callable. A value whose own `constructor.isBuffer` is a non-function makes `qs` call a non-callable and throw `TypeError`. Such a value is produced **by `qs.parse` itself** from an untrusted query string when `plainObjects: true` or `allowPrototypes: true` is set, so a pure-`qs` `parse` → `stringify` round-trip — no `JSON.parse` — turns an unauthenticated query str

expect.note: qs 6.15.1 is the copy nested under body-parser, which loads it only for the extended urlencoded parser (body-parser lib/types/urlencoded.js:137,239-240); app.js:28 sets extended:false (querystring parser), so this copy is never loaded. Even if it were, body-parser only calls qs.parse, never stringify.
expect.labelled_by: claude-opus code read 2026-10-16 (blind: before any judge run; agent-labelled)

facts.advisory_summary: semver vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service — Versions of the package semver before 7.5.2 on the 7.x branch, before 6.3.1 on the 6.x branch, and all other versions before 5.7.2 are vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) via the function new Range, when untrusted user data is provided as a range.

expect.note: semver 7.0.0 (lockfile dev:true) is nested under simple-update-notifier, pulled only by nodemon (devDependency). The server never loads it, and the ranges it compares are package versions, not attacker data.
